# UICC, USIM and the card interface: compliance register

What this is: the requirements of this area that are built and verified against running code, the typed rows recorded while building them, and coverage counts derived from the specs (verification.md §5). Requirements are in [`requirements.md`](../../requirements.md); deviations in [`deviations.md`](../deviations.md).

Specs read: TS 102.221 18.04.00, TS 31.101 j00, TS 31.102 j60.

Row suffixes (requirements.md): -D defect in the sim, -B a choice the spec leaves open, -G declared gap, -V deviation from a "shall", -S spec contradiction and the reading chosen, -M mutant, -T T0 reading or measurement, -F a kaluza-core defect the sim found, -X retired. Verification: U unit, KAT or oracle test; F fuzz or property test; I interop; L lab; G gate row; A real-device comparison.

| KS-UICC-B9 | 2026-10-15 | The card's APDU trace (uicc/trace, P1 N14; sim-uicc.md section 6). Records are APDUs: an answer of 61xx or 6Cxx is held per channel and merged with the GET RESPONSE (or the command sent again) that follows, the command's Le dropped; a held exchange not followed up goes out as it was. Why: pySim-trace's gsmtap-udp source passes each record to its decoder as a whole APDU, without the T=0 filter its library has, so a SELECT answered 61xx counted as failed and its file state was lost (57 unknown FIDs in a dump). Redaction: CK, IK and Kc in AUTHENTICATE answers (straight or through GET RESPONSE) zeroed with RES kept; PIN command data as 'FF'; reads and writes of the key files (os::key_fid: EF.KEYS, EF.KEYSPS, 4F03, 4F04, 4F05, AF20, AF30) zeroed, by FID or by SFI in the ADF and DF.5GS, an SFI elsewhere in a DF.5x masked when unsure; lengths kept so the record decodes.
